description.sr_latin: Kancelarijski razgovori, programerski humor, i kako da preživiš standup na srpskom.
description.en: Office chat, developer humor, and how to survive standup in Serbian.

phrases.sr_latin: Imam bag i ne mogu da skontam odakle dolazi.
phrases.sr_cyrillic: Имам баг и не могу да сконтам одакле долази.
phrases.en: I've got a bug and I can't figure out where it's coming from.
phrases.context: Classic dev frustration. 'Skontam' is slang for 'figure out'.
phrases.notes: 'Bag' is the Serbianized spelling of 'bug'. Tech loanwords are everywhere.

phrases.context: The universal developer excuse, Serbian edition.
phrases.notes: 'Računar' = computer. This phrase transcends all languages.

phrases.context: Looking at terrible code and questioning humanity. Usually the answer is yourself, six months ago.
Letting the team know you're deploying. 'Puštam' literally means 'I'm releasing/letting go'.
phrases.notes: 'Deploy' stays in English in most Serbian dev teams.

phrases.context: The sacred rule of software development, applicable in all languages.
phrases.notes: 'Brate' (bro/brother) is used constantly in casual Serbian speech.

phrases.context: Production is down. Panic mode activated.
phrases.notes: 'Pukao' literally means 'burst/exploded'. Very dramatic, very Serbian.

phrases.context: When the deploy goes wrong and you need to revert.
phrases.notes: Serbian devs freely verb-ify English tech terms by adding Serbian verb endings.

phrases.context: The most important phrase in any Serbian workplace. Coffee breaks are sacred.
Announcing a quick break. Will inevitably last 20 minutes.

phrases.sr_latin: Bez kafe ne mogu da funkcionišem.
phrases.sr_cyrillic: Без кафе не могу да функционишем.
phrases.context: A statement of fact, not a complaint. Universal among Serbian devs.

phrases.en: What are you working on today?
phrases.context: Classic standup question.

phrases.sr_latin: Radim na onom tiketu od juče.
phrases.sr_cyrillic: Радим на оном тикету од јуче.
phrases.en: I'm working on that ticket from yesterday.
phrases.context: Standard standup update. 'Tiket' = ticket (Jira, etc.).

phrases.en: I'm blocked, waiting for a review.
phrases.context: When you can't proceed without someone else's input.

phrases.sr_latin: Opet meeting? Pa kad ću da radim?
phrases.sr_cyrillic: Опет meeting? Па кад ћу да радим?
phrases.en: Another meeting? When am I supposed to work?
phrases.context: The universal developer complaint about too many meetings.
phrases.notes: 'Pa' is a filler word like 'well' or 'so', used for emphasis here.

phrases.context: Asking a colleague to verify something works on their end.

phrases.sr_latin: Probaj sad, trebalo bi da radi.
phrases.sr_cyrillic: Пробај сад, требало би да ради.
phrases.context: After you've pushed a fix and you're hoping for the best.
When the fix didn't fix it.
Every weekday except Friday.
phrases.notes: 'Jedva čekam' literally means 'I barely wait' — used for 'I can't wait'.

phrases.context: The Friday celebration announcement.
The Monday dread that transcends all cultures.

phrases.en: The weekend is always too short.
phrases.context: Monday morning wisdom.
Suggesting a lunch break with colleagues.
The daily lunch debate.
When you packed lunch. Use 'Donela sam' if female.

variations.sr_latin: Danas sam štedljiv, jedem od kuće.
variations.sr_cyrillic: Данас сам штедљив, једем од куће.
variations.en: I'm being frugal today, eating from home.

phrases.context: When the ERP system crashes, which it always does.
phrases.notes: 'Klasika' = 'classic' — used sarcastically when something predictably goes wrong.

phrases.sr_latin: Ne diraj bazu dok traje migracija!
phrases.sr_cyrillic: Не дирај базу док траје миграција!
phrases.en: Don't touch the database during migration!
phrases.context: Yelling at a colleague during a data migration. 'Baza' = database.

phrases.sr_latin: Ko je menjao šemu bez da mi kaže?
phrases.sr_cyrillic: Ко је мењао шему без да ми каже?
phrases.en: Who changed the schema without telling me?
phrases.context: Backend dev rage when someone modifies the database schema.

phrases.en: Did you finish the PIM integration?
phrases.context: Asking about product information management system integration.
phrases.notes: 'Sa PIM-om' — Serbian adds case endings even to acronyms.

phrases.context: Signing off at the end of the work day. Use 'Gotova sam' if female.

phrases.en: Pushing the PR and then I'm out.
phrases.context: Last thing before leaving — submit that pull request.

phrases.sr_latin: Vidimo se sutra. Ako preživi prod.
phrases.sr_cyrillic: Видимо се сутра. Ако преживи прод.
phrases.en: See you tomorrow. If prod survives.
phrases.context: A darkly humorous goodbye after a sketchy deploy.
Checking in on someone's work without being pushy.
Reassuring someone you're making progress at your own pace.
phrases.notes: 'Polako' is quintessentially Serbian — it means 'slowly/easy/chill'. It's both a philosophy and a response.

phrases.sr_latin: Možeš da mi pomogneš sa nečim?
phrases.sr_cyrillic: Можеш да ми помогнеш са нечим?
phrases.en: Can you help me with something?
phrases.context: Asking a colleague for help.
Complaining about a difficult or tedious task.
phrases.notes: 'Ubija' = 'kills'. Serbian loves dramatic expressions for mundane frustrations.
